title: Understanding Cleanroom Classifications: ISO 14644 and Federal Standards
content:
# Understanding Cleanroom Classifications

Cleanrooms are classified by the concentration of airborne particles allowed per cubic metre of air. The two dominant standards are **ISO 14644-1** and the legacy **US Federal Standard 209E**.

## ISO Classes at a Glance

| ISO Class | Max particles ≥0.1 µm/m³ | Equivalent Fed Std |
|-----------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| ISO 1     | 10                       | —                   |
| ISO 3     | 1,000                    | Class 1             |
| ISO 4     | 10,000                   | Class 10            |
| ISO 5     | 100,000                  | Class 100           |
| ISO 6     | 1,000,000                | Class 1,000         |
| ISO 7     | 10,000,000               | Class 10,000        |

## Choosing the Right Consumables

Each ISO class demands consumables processed and packaged in an equal or cleaner environment. For ISO 4 and below, KnightClean gloves, wipes, and garments are processed in our ISO 4 cleanroom facility — ensuring your production environment stays uncontaminated.

## Key Takeaways

- Match your consumable's cleanroom process class to your production class.
- Look for LPC (Liquid Particle Count) and NVR (Non-Volatile Residue) certifications.
- Double-bag packaging adds a layer of contamination protection during transport.

title: How to Choose the Right Cleanroom Gloves for Your Application
content:
# Choosing the Right Cleanroom Gloves

Gloves are the most-changed consumable in any cleanroom. Selecting the wrong type can introduce particles, extractables, or chemical contamination — so the decision matters.

## Material Options

### Nitrile
The most common choice for general cleanroom use. Powder-free nitrile gloves offer excellent chemical resistance to solvents, acids, and bases. Low in particulates and extractables. Suitable for ISO Class 5 and above.

### Latex
Superior tactile sensitivity. Avoid where latex allergies are a concern. Less chemical resistant than nitrile.

### Neoprene
High resistance to a broad chemical spectrum. Preferred for handling aggressive solvents in chemical and pharmaceutical environments.

### Polyisoprene
Latex-free with latex-like feel. Used in pharmaceutical and medical device assembly where sensitivity is critical.

## Key Specifications to Check

- **AQL (Acceptable Quality Level):** AQL 1.5 or better for critical applications
- **LPC (Liquid Particle Count):** particles ≥0.5 µm per cm²
- **NVR (Non-Volatile Residue):** µg/cm² — lower is better
- **ESD properties:** Required for semiconductor and electronics

## InOut Recommendation

For ISO 4–6 semiconductor and electronics work, the **KnightClean TC-TQ12** nitrile gloves (AQL 1.5, chlorinated, anti-static, packed in ISO 4) deliver the contamination control you need.

title: A Practical Guide to Loctite Threadlocking Compounds
content:
# Loctite Threadlocking: Which Grade Do You Need?

Threadlocking adhesives prevent fasteners from loosening due to vibration. Choosing the right grade determines whether you can disassemble later — or at all.

## Strength Grades

| Colour | Grade | Removal | Typical Use |
|--------|-------|---------|-------------|
| Purple | 222   | Hand tools | Small fasteners, instruments |
| Blue   | 243   | Hand tools | General maintenance, M6–M20 |
| Red    | 271   | Heat required | Permanent assemblies, studs |
| Green  | 290   | Hand tools | Wicking into pre-assembled joints |

## Application Tips

1. **Clean and degrease** threads — use Loctite SF 7063 for best adhesion.
2. **Apply to male thread** — one or two drops are sufficient.
3. **Allow full cure** — typically 24 hours at room temperature; use SF 7109 accelerator to speed up curing.
4. **Temperature:** Most threadlockers are effective from -55°C to +150°C.

## When to Use an Activator

Passive metals (stainless steel, zinc-plated steel) cure slowly with anaerobic adhesives. Apply **Loctite SF 7649** primer or **SF 7109** accelerator to the female thread for reliable cure in under 10 minutes.

title: PPE Compliance in Singapore: What Manufacturers Need to Know
content:
# PPE Compliance in Singapore

Workplace safety in Singapore is governed by the **Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Act** and associated regulations enforced by the **Ministry of Manpower (MOM)**. For manufacturers, selecting compliant PPE is both a legal and operational imperative.

## Key Regulatory Standards

### Head Protection
- Hard hats must meet **ANSI/ISEA Z89.1** (Type I/II, Class E/G/C) or **EN 397**.
- Bullard C33 and AboveView™ helmets are rated Type I, Class E and G — suitable for construction, utilities, and general site work.

### Eye and Face Protection
- Protective eyewear should comply with **ANSI Z87.1** or **EN 166**.
- Safety goggles are required when working with chemicals, flying particles, or laser hazards.

### Respiratory Protection
- For chemical environments, select respirators rated to **EN 149 (FFP2/FFP3)** or **NIOSH N95/P100**.
- Surgical-style face masks (Cleanera 3-ply) are suitable for particle control, not chemical vapours.

## Buyer Checklist

- [ ] Verify certifications listed on the product datasheet.
- [ ] Ensure PPE is appropriate for the specific hazard (impact, chemical, electrical).
- [ ] Inspect PPE before each use and replace after any impact or damage.
- [ ] Keep records of PPE issue, inspection, and replacement.

title: Cleanroom Wipes: Polyester, Microfibre, or Cellulose?
content:
# Cleanroom Wipes: Which Material Is Right?

Not all cleanroom wipes are created equal. The substrate material determines particle generation, liquid absorption, solvent compatibility, and the ISO class the wipe is suitable for.

## Material Comparison

### Polyester Knit (e.g. KnightClean TC series)
- **Best for:** ISO Class 3–5
- Very low particle and fibre generation
- Excellent solvent resistance (acetone, IPA, MEK)
- Can be autoclaved
- Higher cost — use where contamination risk is highest

### Microfibre Blend (Polyester/Nylon)
- **Best for:** ISO Class 5–7
- Superior liquid pick-up and retention
- Low lint, high absorbency
- Good for general surface wiping and spill control

### Non-woven Cellulose/Polyester
- **Best for:** ISO Class 6–8 or general industrial
- High absorbency, biodegradable options available
- Higher particle and fibre count than knit polyester
- Cost-effective for high-volume applications

## Common Sizes and Formats

- **5" × 5"** — component handling, spot cleaning
- **9" × 9"** — general surface wiping
- **12" × 12"** — equipment cleaning, large surface areas

## Selection Summary

For critical ISO 4–5 semiconductor or pharmaceutical processes, choose knit polyester. For ISO 6–7 electronics assembly, a quality microfibre blend balances performance and cost.
